questions.q: What is 0.000 456 in standard form?
questions.why: Move the decimal point 4 places right: 4.56 × 10⁻⁴.

questions.q: Round 3.0496 to 3 significant figures.
questions.why: The third significant figure is 4, followed by 9, so it rounds up to 3.05.

questions.q: A price rises from $80 to $92. What is the percentage increase?
questions.why: Increase ÷ original × 100 = 12 ÷ 80 × 100 = 15%.

questions.q: What is the highest common factor of 36 and 60?
$2000 is invested at 5% compound interest per year. What is it worth after 2 years?
Which is irrational?
questions.why: √2 can't be written as a fraction of integers; √16 = 4.

questions.q: Round each number to 1 significant figure to estimate 48.7 × 3.12 ÷ 0.495.
questions.why: Examiners (2023): many put the given numbers into a calculator and rounded the answer. Estimate from 50 × 3 ÷ 0.5 = 300.

questions.q: Which of these is the smallest: 7%, 0.0704, 1/14, 0.0699?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): some treated 7% as the largest, and close values were not checked to enough digits. As decimals: 0.07, 0.0704, 0.0714…, 0.0699.

long.q: Write 0.000 384 in standard form. Work out (3 × 10⁵) × (4 × 10⁻²), giving your answer in standard form.

Priya invests $4500 at a rate of 3.2% per year compound interest. (a) Calculate the value of her investment at the end of 6 years. (b) Find the number of complete years it takes for the investment to first exceed $6000.

In a sale, the price of a jacket is reduced by 15% to $646. (a) Find the original price of the jacket. (b) The shop bought the jacket for $500. Calculate the percentage profit the shop makes when it sells the jacket for $646.
Without using a calculator: (a) simplify √75 − √12, (b) write 6/(3 − √3) in the form a + √b, (c) find the value of 27^(−2/3).
scheme: M1: multiply numerator and denominator by (3 + √3): 6(3 + √3)/(9 − 3)

long.q: A rectangle has length 12.4 cm, correct to the nearest 0.1 cm, and width 7 cm, correct to the nearest centimetre. Calculate (a) the upper bound of the area of the rectangle, (b) the lower bound of its perimeter.
scheme: B1: lower bound of perimeter = 2(12.35 + 6.5) = 37.7 cm

questions.q: Solve 3x − 7 = 11.
Factorise x² + 5x + 6.
questions.why: Find two numbers that multiply to 6 and add to 5: 2 and 3.

questions.q: Expand and simplify (x + 4)(x − 2).
Simplify (2x³)².
questions.why: Square both parts: 2² = 4 and (x³)² = x⁶.

questions.q: Make t the subject of v = u + at.
questions.why: Subtract u, then divide by a.

questions.q: Solve the simultaneous equations x + y = 10 and x − y = 4.
questions.why: Adding gives 2x = 14, so x = 7 and y = 3.

long.q: Solve the simultaneous equations 3x + 2y = 12 and x − y = −1.
Solve the equation 2x² − 5x − 4 = 0, showing all your working and giving your answers correct to 2 decimal places.
Simplify fully (x² − 9)/(2x² + 5x − 3).
f(x) = 3x − 2 and g(x) = x² + 1. (a) Find gf(2). (b) Find f⁻¹(x). (c) Solve ff(x) = 13.
The first five terms of a sequence are 5, 11, 21, 35, 53. (a) Find an expression for the nth term. (b) Show that 203 is a term of the sequence and state which term it is.
scheme: M1: second differences are 4, so the nth term contains 2n²
A1: n = 10, so 203 is the 10th term

questions.q: What is the gradient of the line through (1, 2) and (3, 8)?
What is the y-intercept of y = 4x − 5?
questions.why: In y = mx + c, c is the y-intercept.

questions.q: A line is perpendicular to y = 2x + 1. What is its gradient?
questions.why: Perpendicular gradients multiply to −1.

questions.q: What is the midpoint of (2, 3) and (8, 7)?
questions.why: Average the coordinates: ((2 + 8)/2, (3 + 7)/2) = (5, 5).

questions.q: A line has gradient 2/3. What is the gradient of a line perpendicular to it?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): many drew a parallel line instead of a perpendicular one. Perpendicular gradients multiply to −1.

long.q: Find the gradient and the y-intercept of the line 2y − 6x = 8.

A is the point (−1, 7) and B is the point (3, −1). Find (a) the equation of the line AB in the form y = mx + c, (b) the coordinates of the midpoint of AB, (c) the length of AB, correct to 3 significant figures.
Find the equation of the line that passes through (4, 1) and is perpendicular to the line y = 2x − 3. Find the coordinates of the point where the two lines meet.

The line L has equation 3x + 4y = 24. (a) Find the coordinates of the points where L crosses the x-axis and the y-axis. (b) Find the area of the triangle formed by L and the two axes. (c) Find the gradient of L.
Find the equation of the line through (−2, 3) that is parallel to the line 2x − 5y = 7. Give your answer in the form ax + by = c.

questions.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?
The angle in a semicircle is…
questions.why: An angle subtended by a diameter at the circumference is a right angle.

questions.q: Alternate angles on parallel lines are…
questions.why: Alternate (Z) angles are equal; co-interior angles add to 180°.

questions.q: A tangent meets a radius at the point of contact at…
questions.why: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at that point.

questions.q: A bearing is measured from north in which direction?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): a common error was measuring anticlockwise. Bearings go clockwise from north, written with three figures.

long.q: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 156°. How many sides does the polygon have?
ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. Angle DAB = (2x + 10)° and angle BCD = (3x − 5)°. Find the value of x and the size of angle DAB, giving a reason.
scheme: B1: opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°

long.q: A and B are points on a circle with centre O. The tangents to the circle at A and B meet at the point T, and angle ATB = 48°. Find angle AOB and angle OAB, giving reasons.
scheme: B1: angle OAT = angle OBT = 90° because a tangent is perpendicular to the radius
M1: triangle OAB is isosceles because OA = OB (radii)

long.q: Two bottles are mathematically similar. The smaller bottle has height 12 cm and volume 320 cm³. The larger bottle has height 18 cm and surface area 405 cm². Calculate the volume of the larger bottle and the surface area of the smaller bottle.
scheme: M1: area scale factor (12/18)² or divide by 2.25

long.q: A, B and C are points on a circle with centre O, and AB is a diameter. Angle CAB = 34°. The tangent to the circle at C meets AB extended beyond B at the point T. Find, giving a reason for each, (a) angle ACB, (b) angle ABC, (c) angle BCT, (d) angle CTB.
scheme: B1: angle ACB = 90° (angle in a semicircle)
B1: angle ABC = 180° − 90° − 34° = 56° (angles in a triangle)
M1: angle CBT = 180° − 56° = 124° (angles on a straight line), then angles in triangle BCT

questions.q: What is the area of a circle of radius 5 cm? (π ≈ 3.14)
What is the volume of a cuboid 3 cm by 4 cm by 5 cm?
A triangle has base 10 cm and height 6 cm. What is its area?
questions.why: ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 cm².

questions.q: How many cm² are in 1 m²?
A sector of a circle has radius 6 cm and angle 60°. What is its arc length? (Use π = 3.142)
questions.why: Arc length = (60/360) × 2π × 6 = 2π ≈ 6.28 cm. 37.7 cm is the whole circumference and 18.8 is the sector's area in cm².

long.q: A cylinder has radius 5 cm and height 12 cm. Find its volume and its total surface area, giving each answer correct to 3 significant figures.
A sector of a circle has radius 9 cm and angle 140°. Calculate the perimeter and the area of the sector.
A solid cone has base radius 6 cm and slant height 10 cm. Calculate (a) the vertical height of the cone, (b) the volume of the cone, (c) the curved surface area of the cone.
scheme: B1: curved surface area = π × 6 × 10 = 188 cm²

long.q: A solid metal sphere of radius 3 cm is melted down and recast, with no metal wasted, into a solid cylinder of radius 2 cm. Find the height of the cylinder.
scheme: M1: volume of sphere = 4/3 × π × 3³ = 36π cm³

long.q: A water trough is a prism of length 2.5 m. Its cross-section is a trapezium with parallel sides 40 cm and 60 cm and perpendicular height 30 cm. (a) Calculate the capacity of the trough in litres. (b) The empty trough is filled at a rate of 12 litres per minute. Find the time taken to fill it, in minutes and seconds.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has legs 6 cm and 8 cm. How long is the hypotenuse?
Which ratio is tan θ in a right-angled triangle?
questions.why: SOH CAH TOA: tan = opposite ÷ adjacent.

questions.q: In a triangle, a = 7, b = 5 and the angle C between them is 60°. Which rule finds side c?
questions.why: Two sides and the included angle: c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C.

questions.q: What is the area of a triangle with sides 4 and 9 and an included angle of 30°?
questions.why: Area = ½ab sin C = ½ × 4 × 9 × 0.5 = 9.

questions.q: From a point 20 m from the foot of a tree, the angle of elevation of the top is 35°. How tall is the tree, to 3 significant figures?
questions.why: The height is opposite the angle and 20 m is adjacent, so h = 20 × tan 35° ≈ 14.0 m. Using sin or cos, or dividing by tan, gives the other values.

long.q: In the right-angled triangle ABC, angle ACB = 90°, AB = 13 cm and BC = 5 cm. Calculate angle BAC and the length AC.
In triangle ABC, AB = 8.5 cm, angle ACB = 47° and angle ABC = 68°. Calculate the length of AC and the area of the triangle.
A triangle has sides of length 7 cm, 9 cm and 12 cm. Calculate the size of its largest angle.
scheme: M1: largest angle is opposite the 12 cm side: cos θ = (7² + 9² − 12²)/(2 × 7 × 9)

long.q: A ship sails 14 km from port P on a bearing of 060° to a point Q. It then sails 9 km on a bearing of 150° to a point R. (a) Explain why angle PQR = 90°. (b) Calculate the distance PR. (c) Calculate the bearing of R from P.
scheme: B1: the bearing of P from Q is 240°, and 240° − 150° = 90°

long.q: A cuboid has a rectangular base 8 cm by 6 cm and a height of 5 cm. Calculate (a) the length of the diagonal of the base, (b) the angle between a space diagonal of the cuboid and its base, (c) the length of the space diagonal.

questions.q: Shape A is enlarged by scale factor 3. How do the areas compare?
questions.why: Area scale factor = (length scale factor)² = 9.

questions.q: Which transformation keeps a shape the same size but turns it?
questions.why: A rotation turns a shape about a centre; size and shape are unchanged.

questions.q: What is the magnitude of the vector (3, 4)?
The point (2, 5) is reflected in the line y = x. What are the coordinates of its image?
questions.why: Reflecting in y = x swaps the coordinates, so (2, 5) maps to (5, 2).

questions.q: The point (3, 1) is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of its image?
questions.why: A 90° clockwise rotation about the origin maps (x, y) to (y, −x), so (3, 1) goes to (1, −3). (−1, 3) is the anticlockwise image and (−3, −1) is a half turn.

long.q: a is the column vector (3, −2) and b is the column vector (−1, 4). Find 2a − b and |2a − b|.
Triangle T has vertices (2, 1), (5, 1) and (5, 3). Triangle U has vertices (1, −2), (1, −5) and (3, −5). Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle T onto triangle U.

Triangle A has vertices (2, 2), (6, 2) and (2, 4). Triangle B has vertices (1, 1), (3, 1) and (1, 2). (a) Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle A onto triangle B. (b) Find the area of triangle B.
scheme: B1: area of B = ½ × 2 × 1 = 1 unit² (a quarter of the area of A, which is 4 units²)
long.ans: enlargement, scale factor ½, centre (0, 0); 1 unit²

long.q: OABC is a parallelogram with OA = a and OC = c. M is the midpoint of AB. P is the point on OM such that OP : PM = 2 : 1. (a) Find OM and OP in terms of a and c. (b) Find CP in terms of a and c and hence show that P lies on the line CA, stating the ratio CP : PA.
scheme: A1: CP = ⅔a − ⅔c = ⅔(a − c)
A1: CA = a − c, so CP = ⅔CA: P lies on CA and CP : PA = 2 : 1
long.ans: a + ½c; ⅔a + ⅓c; ⅔(a − c); 2 : 1

long.q: p is the column vector (4, k) and q is the column vector (6, −9). Given that p is parallel to q, find the value of k and the number t for which p = tq.

questions.q: A fair die is rolled. What is the probability of a number greater than 4?
questions.why: 5 and 6 are 2 of 6 outcomes: 2/6 = 1/3.

questions.q: P(rain) = 0.3. What is P(no rain)?
questions.why: Probabilities of all outcomes add to 1: 1 − 0.3 = 0.7.

questions.q: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of two heads?
questions.why: Independent events multiply: ½ × ½ = ¼.

questions.q: A bag has 3 red and 2 blue balls. Two are taken without replacement. P(both red)?
A biased coin lands on heads with probability 0.6. It is thrown 50 times. How many heads would you expect?
questions.why: Expected frequency = probability × number of trials = 0.6 × 50 = 30. 25 would be expected only for a fair coin.

long.q: A spinner lands on red with probability 0.35. It is spun twice. Find the probability that it lands on red exactly once.

A bag contains 5 red counters and 3 blue counters. Two counters are taken at random without replacement. Find the probability that (a) both counters are the same colour, (b) at least one counter is blue.

In a class of 40 students, 23 study French, 18 study Spanish and 7 study neither language. (a) Find the number of students who study both languages. (b) A student is chosen at random. Find the probability that the student studies French only. (c) A student who studies French is chosen at random. Find the probability that this student also studies Spanish.
scheme: M1: 23 + 18 − x + 7 = 40, or use a Venn diagram

long.q: A biased six-sided dice is thrown. The probability of a 6 is 0.15, the probability of a 5 is 0.2 and the numbers 1, 2, 3 and 4 are equally likely. (a) Find the probability of throwing a 1. (b) The dice is thrown 300 times. Find the expected number of 6s.

The probability that it rains on a Monday is 0.3. If it rains, the probability that Sam is late for school is 0.4; if it does not rain, the probability that he is late is 0.1. (a) Find the probability that Sam is late on a Monday. (b) Given that Sam is late on a Monday, find the probability that it rained.

questions.q: What is the median of 3, 7, 2, 9, 5?
questions.why: In order: 2, 3, 5, 7, 9; the middle value is 5.

questions.q: What is the mean of 4, 6, 8, 10?
questions.why: Total 28 ÷ 4 values = 7.

questions.q: A scatter graph shows points rising from left to right. This is…
questions.why: As one variable increases, so does the other.

questions.q: In a histogram, the height of each bar shows…
questions.why: Frequency density = frequency ÷ class width, so the area shows frequency.

questions.q: 20 students were asked how many pets they own: 5 own 0, 8 own 1, 4 own 2 and 3 own 3. What is the mean number of pets per student?
questions.why: Total pets = 0×5 + 1×8 + 2×4 + 3×3 = 25, and 25 ÷ 20 = 1.25. 1 is the mode and median, and 1.5 is just the mean of 0, 1, 2 and 3.

long.q: The mean of 6 numbers is 14. A seventh number is added and the mean becomes 15. Find the seventh number.

The heights of 40 plants are recorded. 6 plants have height h cm with 140 < h ≤ 150, 14 have 150 < h ≤ 160, 15 have 160 < h ≤ 170 and 5 have 170 < h ≤ 180. (a) Write down the modal class. (b) Calculate an estimate of the mean height.

The times, t minutes, that 54 people waited for a bus are grouped as follows: 12 people with 0 < t ≤ 10, 18 people with 10 < t ≤ 15 and 24 people with 15 < t ≤ 30. Calculate the frequency density of each class, ready to draw a histogram.
scheme: M1: frequency density = frequency ÷ class width

long.q: 80 students took a test marked out of 100. The cumulative frequencies are: mark ≤ 20: 6, mark ≤ 40: 22, mark ≤ 60: 50, mark ≤ 80: 72, mark ≤ 100: 80. (a) Find how many students scored more than 60. (b) Estimate the median mark, assuming the marks are spread evenly within each class (or from a cumulative frequency curve).
scheme: B1: the median is the 40th value, which lies in the class 40 < mark ≤ 60
A1: about 53 (accept 51 to 55 from a curve)

long.q: The number of goals scored in 20 football matches is recorded: 0 goals in 5 matches, 1 goal in 8 matches, 2 goals in 4 matches, 3 goals in 2 matches and 4 goals in 1 match. Find the mean, the median, the mode and the range of the number of goals.
scheme: B1: median = 1 (the 10th and 11th values are both 1)
